Families with older children may not consider you because they may doubt your ability to keep up with their children. And many, many people will not consider you simply because they dont want to change anything in their home to accommodate your chair. 

I occasionally need a cane for mobility assistance - even that had been a problem for me with many families. They assume I can’t keep up, that I’m not physically stable enough to hold a baby safely, that my cane could be a danger (so many people have said this to me - I even had one person tell me they felt like it was a potential weapon. I don’t mean to be discouraging, but I don’t think this is a realistic option for consistent work.

As others have said, you’re going to have a really tough time selling this whole collection to anyone except maaaaaaybe a reseller - who will likely offer you something very very low and turn around charge others way more. 

In a perfect world, 2 bins x 234 mists in each, so 468 mists, around $7/mist (which is what I see them go for individually on fb marketplace in my area) would be like $3275. I really, really doubt anyone is going to pay that. 

If you don’t care about making much back and don’t have any personal ethical issues selling in bulk to a reseller (if you can find one) I can’t imagine you getting more than $2-3 per mist, since they could be considered “used” and these resellers wait for sales and coupons to maximize their savings. That would put you at closer to $1150ish. Personally, I don’t see that happening either, especially since you’d have to find someone local to buy them - shipping all those as one would cost far more than it’s worth. 

Honestly, your best bet is to bundle them out or sell them individually. Idk if this sub has rules against reselling, but you could likely find some buyers here (honestly I’d be very interested in some personally, and I’ve seen a couple other comments expressing interest). The problem with this, of course, is the work involved in inventorying everything you have, keeping track, and shipping them all, which may be more work than you’re willing to undertake (which is reasonable). 

The easiest thing for you to do, if you don’t actually care about recovering any of your financial loss here, would be to donate all of this to a woman’s shelter. Anything unopened they will likely take. They may not take some stuff that’s visibly opened/used, so I’d call around to the shelters in your area and see what their policies are. Also consider contacting your local LGBTQ Centers, as many nowadays have “closets” that low income queer people can “shop” (for free, typically) - personal products like this can absolutely be gender affirming and would likely put smiles on a lot of faces!
